clue.text: Hateful chap and others swapping tips for trial

indicators.note: the front ends of the two words trade places, so their opening letters are exchanged

parts.note: a toad is a loathsome person
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a nasty character and his companions by having them change places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping tips' exchanges the first letters of TOAD and REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A road test is a trial of a vehicle or product under real working conditions.

clue.text: Old country's rugby obsession

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
a mania is an obsession

explanation.surface: A former nation is said to be fixated on rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumania is an old spelling of the Balkan state now usually written Romania.

clue.text: Make light of everything, having strayed out of bounds

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: the bounds are the outer letters, which are put out of the word

parts.note: deviated means strayed from the path

explanation.surface: Someone treats everything lightly after wandering off where they should not go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of bounds' removes the first and last letters of DEVIATED, leaving EVIATE; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten a burden or pain is to ease it, the sense of relieving suffering.

clue.text: Repentant Richelieu's embrace of Eastern mysticism

indicators.note: the run of words holds the solution in its arms, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A penitent French cardinal takes up oriental spiritual practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantric describes the tantra tradition of Hindu and Buddhist esoteric ritual and meditation.

clue.text: Concealment and seclusion, firstly and secondly, required before battle

indicators.note: the opening piece must stand ahead of the next
only the letters standing first and second in the word are taken

parts.note: Crecy was the 1346 English victory over the French

explanation.surface: Hiding away in privacy is called for before going to war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firstly and secondly' takes SE, the first two letters of 'seclusion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Secrecy is the state of keeping things hidden, which is what concealment means.

clue.text: He likes to talk and joke around when with bishop

indicators.note: the joke word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a gag is a joke
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A man fond of chatting jokes about with a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is a garrulous person who talks too much.

clue.text: Irregular for the most part involved with Left

definitions.text: Irregular for the most part involved with Left

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up together into a new order
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: An irregular fighter is mostly mixed up with left-wing politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts IRREGULAR to IRREGULA; 'involved' scrambles that with L.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular soldier, and many guerrilla movements have been of the political left.

clue.text: Woman with sock business

parts.note: she is a woman
to sock is to hit, as is to bang

explanation.surface: A woman with a punch runs her affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang means an affair or matter, as in 'the whole shebang'.

clue.text: Greek department famous for ego therein

definitions.meaning: a regional unit of the Peloponnese in Greece
the Latin motto 'Et in ... ego', 'I too am there', names this place

explanation.surface: A Greek region is known for the self-regard of its people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Et in Arcadia ego' is the famous Latin tag on a tomb in Poussin's painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a Greek administrative area, and the pastoral land of the celebrated Latin phrase.

clue.text: Once tamely submitted to torture in darkening cell

indicators.note: letters put through torment are twisted out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone once docile was tortured in a dark prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A melanocyte is a skin cell that makes melanin, the pigment that darkens skin.

clue.text: Heroin and so forth previously cut with acid

indicators.note: the second piece comes earlier than the drug letter

parts.note: etc is the abbreviation for et cetera, and so forth
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Heroin and other drugs were adulterated with acid beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a surface by letting acid eat into it.

clue.text: Get to succeed not once but twice in imaginary situation

indicators.note: to succeed is to follow, so this piece comes after
the word is written two times over

parts.note: never means not once
to land is to arrive at, get to

explanation.surface: Advice that you will never succeed, however hard you try.
explanation.definitionFit: Never-never land is an idyllic place of fantasy, from Peter Pan.

clue.text: Ban march by leaders out to cause chaos

indicators.note: each word loses its leading letter

explanation.surface: Banning a protest march may stir up disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: Ban, march and by lose their first letters, leaving AN, ARCH, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is lawless disorder, a state of chaos.

clue.text: Am hideous working girl with bad knee?

indicators.note: letters at work are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl wonders if she is ugly while at work and nursing a sore knee.
explanation.walkthrough: Housemaid's knee is inflammation from kneeling, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A housemaid's knee is a bursitis named after servants who scrubbed floors on their knees.

clue.text: Lamenting agile manoeuvring in the City

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the City postcode

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: letters being manoeuvred are moved around into new order

explanation.surface: Someone mourns nimble trading in London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac means mournful, in the manner of an elegy for the dead.

clue.text: Hesitation in plan for burial

indicators.note: the hesitation goes inside the plan word

parts.note: an intent is a plan or purpose
erm is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A pause in the plans for a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Interment is the burying of a body in the ground.

clue.text: Heroic Greek male begs to return after time

indicators.note: the remaining pieces follow the time letter

parts.note: he is a male

indicators.note: the word goes back, read right to left

parts.note: to sue is to beg or plead

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek man pleads to come home after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the hero of Greek myth who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: I refused to mop on a public holiday for non-U Hindu

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after
read as re-fused: the I is joined back on in a new place

parts.note: a mop is a shock of hair
January starts with New Year's Day, a public holiday

explanation.surface: Someone declines to clean up on a bank holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refused', read as re-fused, shifts the I in HAIR to give HARI. 'non-U' plays on untouchable: U is upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Harijan, Gandhi's word, names a Dalit, a Hindu outside the caste system, hence lowly.

clue.text: Second bottle not a cause of suffering

indicators.note: the following word is left out

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.surface: Another bottle is not what causes the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is something that brings affliction, originally a whip.

clue.text: Sided with expert to skewer newspaper boss

indicators.note: the expert pierces the newspaper letters, sitting inside them

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
an ace is an expert
ed is short for editor, the boss of a paper

explanation.surface: An editor teamed up with a skilled hand to attack his own paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Faceted means having faces or sides, like a cut gem.

clue.text: Film director went overboard, one concludes

parts.note: to fall in is to drop into the water
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A director goes over the side and someone wraps things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concludes' places the I at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was an Italian film director, maker of La Dolce Vita.

clue.text: Extremely important, as work is to people

definitions.meaning: op, a short word for work, sits in the middle of the word people

explanation.surface: Something matters greatly, just as having a job matters to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads people as PE-OP-LE: OP (opus, work) is in its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Central means principal or essential, and literally at the middle.

clue.text: Bounced cheque getting George North in indignant state

parts.note: a dud is a worthless cheque

explanation.surface: A rugby player's bad cheque leaves someone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: George North is a Welsh rugby player, which disguises the split.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offended resentment, as in 'high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Layer of rust?

parts.note: a layer is an egg-laying hen, and rust names this breed's reddish plumage

explanation.surface: A coating of corrosion on metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhode Island Red is a chicken breed with rust-red feathers, kept for laying eggs.

clue.text: King from the East is not very open

indicators.note: in an across clue the word is read from the right, the east side

parts.note: a raja is an Indian king

explanation.surface: An oriental monarch is not very forthcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: A door ajar is slightly open, not wide open.

clue.text: Unknown in Tenerife, a compound which prevents ice damage

indicators.note: the unknown goes inside the rearranged letters
to compound is to mix together, so the letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A chemical no one has heard of on the Canary island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' mixes TENERIFE and A; 'in' puts Z among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Antifreeze is added to engine coolant to stop freezing that would crack the block.

clue.text: Setter died in poverty for sure

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the poverty word

parts.note: need is poverty

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler definitely died penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb of emphasis meaning certainly or truly.

clue.text: Tamworth, perhaps, has passionate secret language

parts.note: the Tamworth is a British breed of pig
Latin, as in a Latin temperament, means fiery and passionate

explanation.surface: A town in Staffordshire supposedly has an amorous hidden tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth looks like the English town, but it is a pig breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig Latin is a children's code that moves the first sound of each word to the end.
